question: In relation to the consumption of dietary fiber, it is true that:

options.opa: It must be balanced (25% soluble and 75% insoluble, approximately).
options.opb: The higher the consumption of fiber, the lower the water intake.
options.opc: The products made with refined seeds have a high fiber content.
options.opd: Legumes are a poor source of fiber.
options.ope: In the adult, 10-15 g of fiber are recommended daily.

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Dietary fiber" -> "includes soluble and insoluble types" -> "no specific required ratio" -> "unclear" -> 60%
CHAIN: "High fiber consumption" -> "does not necessarily reduce water intake" -> "hydration is still important" -> "possible" -> 70%
CHAIN: "Refined seeds" -> "typically have lower fiber content" -> "due to processing" -> "false" -> 90%
CHAIN: "Legumes" -> "are known for high fiber content" -> "considered a good source of fiber" -> "false" -> 90%
CHAIN: "Recommended daily fiber intake" -> "is generally 25-30 g for adults" -> "10-15 g is low" -> "false" -> 90%
analysis: Dietary fiber is generally recommended to be consumed in a balanced manner, but the specific ratio of soluble to insoluble fiber is not strictly defined as 25% to 75%. Higher fiber intake typically requires increased water intake to aid digestion, not the opposite. Refined products usually have lower fiber content due to the removal of bran and germ. Legumes are actually a good source of fiber. The recommended daily intake of fiber for adults is generally higher than 10-15 g, with many guidelines suggesting around 25-30 g. Therefore, all options provided are incorrect.
